ARTEFACT: Movable archaeological finds of every kind and groups of finds recovered in archaeological contexts. This includes pottery and ceramic assemblages, tools, jewellery, coin types, figurines, seals, inscriptions, clothing items, objects depicted on artefacts or works of art, architectural members when treated as finds, bones, deposited remains, and parts of artefacts such as «λαβές». Annotate the core artefact noun, not descriptive adjectives unless they form a fixed artefact type or are necessary to identify the object. Examples: «ενώτια», «αλιευτικά δίχτυα». Include the full artefact phrase when the modifier is part of the object name or meaning, e.g. «σκύφου μὲ δακτυλιόσχημη βάση». Do not annotate immovable structures such as tombs, walls, or temples as ARTEFACT. Do not split a complete artefact phrase into FEATURE + ARTEFACT when the whole phrase names the object.
PERIOD: Archaeological periods, chronological phases, cultural phases, and ancient date ranges, such as «Νεολιθική εποχή», «Τελική Νεολιθική», «πρωιμότερη της Πρώιμης Εποχής του Χαλκού», «παλαιότερες τῆς Νεολιθικῆς περιόδους», «β΄ μισό του 3ου αι. μ.Χ.», or «φάση Φυλακωπή IV». Include the full chronological expression, especially when it contains modifiers, centuries, or complex date ranges. For chronological ranges, annotate the entire range as one PERIOD span, including prepositions, conjunctions, and chronological markers such as «από», «έως», «μέχρι», «και μετά», «αι.», «π.Χ.», and «μ.Χ.». Do not annotate the individual dates separately. Examples: «ΥΕ ΙΙΙΒ/Γ», «από το 3600 ως το 3000 π.Χ.», «κατὰ τὴν ἀρχαιότερη φάση», «από τον 8ο αι. π.Χ. μέχρι τον 2ο αι. μ.Χ.». Exclude modern dates, excavation seasons, and modern historical references.
LOCATION: Named geographical places and place names, including cities, villages, regions, countries, mountains, islands, ancient place names, museums, and named archaeological sites when used primarily as toponyms rather than structures. Include complete place-name expressions, especially when they contain personal-name elements, saints' names, genitives, or regional qualifiers. Examples: «Πλωτινόπολη», «Ραμνοῦς», «Ραμνοῦντος», «Δήλος», «Θεολόγος Θάσου», «όρμος του Αγίου Ιωάννη». Distinguish between a person and a location named after a person, e.g. «Άγιος Ιωάννης» as a site. If a phrase names a geographical place or feature, such as a harbour, village, or hill, annotate the entire name as LOCATION. Annotate place names as LOCATION regardless of capitalization. Do not annotate generic geographical nouns alone, such as «νησί», «πλαγιά», or «θέση», unless they are part of a named place expression.
CONTEXT: Immovable archaeological contexts, built spaces, architectural structures, and in situ ancient ruins. This includes temples, sanctuaries, altars, stoas, agoras, cemeteries, deposits, architectural spaces, and structural architectural members when they are part of a building or monument. Prefer the complete meaningful structure span, especially when an adjective or genitive identifies the structure. Examples: «βωμός», «πηγάδι», «ελλειψοειδείς οικίες», «ἀκρόπολη», «Ιερό του Απόλλωνα», «Ιερό», «ἱεροῦ της Ἀφροδίτης Ἡγεμόνης», «Ιερό του Πανός», «θεμέλια τοίχου», «παραστάδες», «επιστύλιο», «γείσο». Distinguish between structural spaces, such as «ιερό» or «ναός», and functional or abstract expressions, such as «θρησκευτικό κέντρο». Do not annotate generic functional expressions as CONTEXT. Do not annotate loose fills or surface deposits such as «ἐπιχώσεις» as CONTEXT unless they are explicitly treated as an archaeological layer or deposit. Do not annotate named geographical places as CONTEXT.
MATERIAL: Specific materials, substances, animal-derived materials, pigments, and material adjectives from which artefacts, structures, or finds are made. Examples: «μάρμαρο», «λίθος», «λίθινα», «πηλός», «άργιλος», «χαλκός», «χρυσός». Annotate material adjectives separately from artefacts when they simply indicate material, e.g. «πήλινων» + «βαριδίων». Do not annotate material words when they are part of a PERIOD expression, e.g. «Χαλκού» in «Πρώιμη Εποχή του Χαλκού». Do not annotate broad generic expressions such as «πρώτες ύλες» unless a specific material is named. If bones, ceramics, or fragments are described as deposited finds rather than as the substance of another object, annotate them as ARTEFACT instead of MATERIAL.
SPECIES: Animal and plant species, including real, symbolic, and mythological animals when they denote living beings or depicted creatures. Include parenthetical or synonymous species terms when present. Examples: «λιοντάρι», «λιονταράκι», «σκύμνος», «φίδι», «γρύπας». If the animal or plant term denotes the material of an object, such as shell or bone, annotate it as MATERIAL instead of SPECIES. Do not annotate personal names, divine figures, or mythological persons as SPECIES.
PERSON: Historical, mythological, divine, religious, or legendary figures mentioned as persons or named beings. Examples: «Αλέξανδρος», «Αλέξανδρος οΜέγας», «Απόλλων», «Απόλλωνα». Include alphabetic numerals, ordinal markers, epithets, and titles when they are part of the personal name, such as «IV», «Β΄». Examples: «Λέων ΣΤ΄ο Σοφός», «Ιουστίνος Β΄». Exclude modern persons, such as archaeologists, researchers, authors, excavators, and scholars. Do not annotate personal-name elements as PERSON when they are part of a place name, such as «Άγιος Ιωάννης Θεολόγου».
FEATURE: Stylistic, typological, iconographic, decorative, technical, morphological, or formal characteristics of artefacts, figures, or artistic representations. Annotate features when they describe decoration, technique, or iconography, but do not over-annotate ordinary descriptive adjectives. Examples: «διάτρητες», «εμπίεση», «ανάγλυφη διακόσμηση», «ανθρωπόμορφα», «ζωόμορφα», «ένθρονη μορφή», «ερυθρόμορφος». Do not annotate simple shape or color adjectives such as «σφαιρικές», «επιμήκεις», or «μονόχρωμος». Do not split a complete artefact expression into FEATURE + ARTEFACT when the modifier is part of the artefact span, e.g. annotate «εγκόλπιος σταυρός» as ARTEFACT, not «εγκόλπιος» as FEATURE plus «σταυρός» as ARTEFACT.
